title: Bottle fill: is the filler running high?
intro:
A filling machine puts sauce into bottles. When it is set correctly the fill weights have mean **μ = 500 g** and standard deviation **σ = 8 g**, close to normal. A technician weighs **n = 16** bottles and finds **x̄ = 503.5 g**.

If the machine is still set correctly, how unusual is a sample mean this high? Find the z-value of x̄ = 503.5 g on the sampling distribution of x̄, and the probability P(x̄ ≥ 503.5). Give z to two decimals and the probability to three decimals or more.

Z.says: You divided by σ = 8 g. That is the z of a single bottle. For the mean of 16 bottles divide by the standard error, σ/√n.

AtLeast.says: That is P(x̄ ≤ 503.5), the area to the left. "At least 503.5" is the area to the right: 1 − Φ(z).
That is the chance that one bottle weighs 503.5 g or more (z from σ). For the mean of 16 bottles use the standard error, σ/√n.

hints: z = (x̄ − μ) / standard error = (503.5 − 500) / standard error.
P(x̄ ≥ 503.5) = 1 − Φ(z), the area to the right of z.
